findings.description: updateLocation recreates calendar references with undefined externalCalendarId/credentialId — These fields are always undefined because `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`, so `editLocation.handler.ts` recreates the booking's references without them and later reschedules/cancels lose the Google event. Fall back to `evt.destinationCalendar` or return both fields from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`.

Team destination calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null — When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, the optional chain silently drops `teamDestinationCalendars`, so COLLECTIVE bookings create no calendar events for hosts that do have destination calendars. Assign with a spread over `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` instead.

Video booking references created with null credentialId, breaking seat-cancellation updates — Video results now get a null `credentialId`, but seat cancellation in `handleCancelBooking.ts` relies on `reference.credentialId` to load the credential and update the meeting, so removed attendees stay in the call. Drop the `isCalendarType` guard and always store `result.credentialId`.

Destructuring destinationCalendar without guard throws on null/empty array — When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and `.integration` throws, breaking the Google Meet without Google Calendar case this check exists for. Add optional chaining to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Dead fallback in updateEvent always yields undefined when externalCalendarId is falsy — In the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy by definition, so `find` can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined, making updates without an external calendar fail instead of using the booking's destination calendar. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`.

Inverted billing condition: slug set on cloud instead of self-hosted — The dropped negation means self-hosted organizations are created without a `slug` while cloud organizations get one immediately, bypassing the `requestedSlug` reservation flow that holds the slug until the organization is published. Restore the negation in the ternary.

Adding guests to seated bookings overbooks slots and skips BookingSeat creation — Attendees get created without seats, so they can't be managed or cancelled per-seat and become invisible in seat-based views. Reject seated bookings early, as the fix does, or create `BookingSeat` rows after checking remaining capacity.

EventManager built with caller's credentials instead of organizer's — When the caller is an attendee or team admin, their credentials get used against the organizer's external calendar event and the update fails, so new guests never appear on it. Build the `EventManager` from `booking.user` instead of `ctx.user`.

Team admins rejected: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner only passes for owners — Team admins who are neither organizer nor attendee get a FORBIDDEN error, contradicting the intent of `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already covers admins and owners, combine the checks with `||` instead of `&&`.

Guest emails with uppercase characters bypass the guest email blocklist — A guest like 'Spam@x.com' gets added and emailed despite being blocked. Compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against `blacklistedGuestEmails`, matching `checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked` which lowercases both sides.

Team bookings build CalendarEvent without team, so team hosts miss guest emails — Additional team-member hosts never receive the guests-added email, and subjects fall back to the organizer's personal name. Populate `team` on `evt` from the booking's event type team, fetching its name and accepted members as `handleNewBooking` does.

Unbounded guests array allows mass attendee/email abuse — A single request can insert thousands of attendee rows and send mass emails to arbitrary third parties through Cal.com's mail infrastructure. Cap the `guests` array with `.max(10)` and consider a per-request limit in the handler.

isInvalidEmail banner never cleared on success, persists across dialog opens — The stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner reappears the next time the dialog opens after a successful add. Reset it with `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` in `onSuccess` and at the start of a passing validation in `handleAdd`.

Booking-ID oracle: distinct NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN errors leak booking existence — Any authenticated user can probe this mutation to enumerate valid booking IDs across the system by comparing the two error responses. Scope the lookup to bookings the caller can access, or return `booking_not_found` for unauthorized IDs too.

Duplicate emails in guests array create duplicate attendee rows — Duplicate attendee rows cause repeated guest emails and duplicate calendar updates, even from concurrent requests. Dedupe the `guests` input case-insensitively in the handler as shown, or add a unique constraint on `Attendee`.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests — Guests already on the booking receive a fresh 'confirmed' invitation with an .ics file even though nothing changed for them. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

Sync-mode refresh responses rejected by strict webexRefreshedTokenSchema — Sync-mode responses only carry an access token and expiry, but `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` demands literal `scope`, `token_type`, and `refresh_token` fields, so every webex refresh rejects and no token is ever persisted. Validate the response with `parseRefreshTokenResponse` like the other adapters do.

Credential key stores parseRefreshTokenResponse wrapper instead of parsed token — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `{ success, data }` safeParse wrapper, so the credential key becomes that wrapper instead of the token, and Google Calendar breaks on the next call after its first refresh. Store `parsedToken.data` as the key, matching the other consumers.

Broken computed keys make token schema strip expiry_date and real refresh_token — The computed keys evaluate to the literal key `[object Object]`, so `z.object` strips `expiry_date` and the real `refresh_token`, and persisting the result wipes the user's stored refresh token. Use a passthrough schema that captures the numeric expiry and never write a placeholder `refresh_token`.

Backup-code comparison is not constant-time, leaking match info via timing — Response times reveal how many leading characters of a submitted `backupCode` match a stored one, which is enough to reconstruct a code that together with the password authenticates the account. Concurrent BuildIndex calls for same key race without per-build serialization — Two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same key now both build: file-backed indexes fail on `bleve.New`'s file lock, memory-only ones leak an index and split writes across instances. Hold `cacheMu` for the whole build so the loser blocks and then hits the cache.

Postgres skip silently drops instrumentation-server coverage and masks a failure — A real, possibly PR-introduced failure (eager `Init` building the search index) is being hidden: the test now skips before exercising the instrumentation server on postgres, so any regression there passes silently. Root-cause and fix the postgres failure, or narrow the skip with a linked issue.

Silence menu item is a no-op: RuleActionsButtons gets no ruler rule to wire silence flow — Users with silence permission click the menu item and nothing opens, since `RuleActionsButtons` renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only when a ruler rule is present, and the list view no longer fetches one. Wire the flow to the prom rule (or a prom-based drawer) and gate the item on the same condition.

isFederated hardcoded to false, federated rule groups lose immutability guard — Federated Mimir rule groups are no longer treated as immutable, so Edit/Delete/Pause become supported through `useAlertRuleAbility` once datasource ruler permissions pass. Keep the `isFederatedRuleGroup` check in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` or thread the group into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` until the TODO is implemented.

`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule()` doesn't narrow `promRule` — `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule()` is a plain boolean check, not a type predicate, so `promRule` stays `Rule | undefined` where `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` is required — a type error here and in `RuleActionsButtons.V2`, whose `promRule.uid` can also read undefined. Export a narrowing guard such as `isGrafanaPromRule` or validate at the boundary so both call sites narrow.

skipToken rules still report supported=true for globally-permitted Grafana prom rule abilities — When the rule is `skipToken`, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` still yields supported for abilities backed by a global permission, so Mimir rules render the Duplicate item without the datasource write permission the ruler path requires. Return NotSupported for every ability while the rule is skipped, so skipped rows produce [false, false].

Cloud rule tests don't exercise permission gating; mocked hook hides buttons — These tests pass even if the new Mimir gating logic is broken, since the stubbed `useIsRuleEditable` omits `isRulerAvailable`, making every ability NotSupported and hiding Edit/Delete regardless of permissions. Let the real hook run, or add `isRulerAvailable: true` to the stub and assert the buttons track permission changes.

Negative Edit-button test passes regardless of which ability hook is consulted — The assertion holds no matter which hook drives the edit decision — `useRulerRuleAbility` stays at its [false, false] default, the same result the denied permission yields — so removing the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` call would still pass. Pin the other hooks to allow so only `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` denying makes the button disappear.

testIncorrectGrantType passes via incidental NPE, not grant-type validation — Catching `RuntimeException` swallows an incidental NPE: `before()` never calls `factory.postInit()`, so `sessionFactory` stays null and the unknown shortcut throws before the intended `IllegalArgumentException`. Assert on `IllegalArgumentException` and initialize the factory so the validation path actually runs.

Constructor guard re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId — A null `rawTokenId` slips through this duplicate `grantType` check and later yields a corrupt token ID like "onrtna:null" in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` instead of failing fast. Make the second check require `rawTokenId`, matching its message.

isAccessTokenId grant check uses wrong substring and inverted polarity, so it never fails — The wrong `substring` bounds and inverted polarity turn this check into a no-op, so token IDs with a wrong or missing grant type still match the event. Use `substring(4, 6)` and return false on mismatch.

Sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads still lack the null guard — The same concurrent-deletion race still throws an NPE through the unguarded `modelSupplier.get()` calls in the three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads, so the fix is only partial. Apply the same null check, or a shared null-safe accessor, at all four call sites.

Reader thread may finish no reads before deletes complete, passing vacuously — On a slow or loaded machine all 100 deletes can finish before the reader thread's first call, so the loop exits having read nothing and the assertion passes vacuously — the race is never exercised. Gate the delete loop on a latch that the reader signals once running.

getSubGroupsCount() returns null, violating GroupModel never-null contract — Callers relying on the `GroupModel` contract ("Never returns null" in server-spi) that unbox the result to a primitive `long` will now hit a fresh NullPointerException. Return a fallback such as `0L`, or document the contract change on the interface.

Reader thread not joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty — A request still in flight when `deletedAll.set(true)` runs can append to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed, hiding the very NPE this test guards against. Keep a reference to the reader thread, join it after the delete loop, then assert.

JS console uses i18next {{n}} interpolation, but new value uses Java ChoiceFormat — The console renders this value with i18next, which ignores single braces and has no choice format, so users will see raw placeholders instead of the attribute name and counts. Use the `{{n}}` form without the choice, as also needed in the account-ui messages file.

Common prefix/suffix scans can overlap, causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — When the prefix scan overlaps the suffix scan, the `sanitized.substring` and `value.substring` calls throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Clamp `end` so suffix and prefix never overlap, for both strings.

Uncaught RuntimeException when English reference file is missing or unresolvable — The RuntimeException from reading the English reference escapes `verify()`, aborting the whole run at the first missing file instead of recording a per-file diagnostic. Skip with a message in `messages` when the reference file is missing or unresolvable.

NPE in hasPermission when Clients type resource does not exist — When the realm's admin-permissions client predates this PR, `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` no-ops and `getResourceTypeResource` returns null, so `findByResource` throws an NPE and every client view or update turns into a 500. Add a null check returning false, mirroring the 1-arg `hasPermission`.

Client delete fails when both fine-grained authz versions enabled: V2 cleanup throws — When both feature flags are on, the handler in AdminPermissions.java selects `MgmtPermissionsV2` and `setPermissionsEnabled` throws, so deleting any client fails and rolls back. Make the guard skip cleanup when the V2 flag is active instead of checking the V1 flag.

Per-client resource lacks type so all-clients policies are ignored in evaluation — An all-clients grant silently stops applying once any per-client permission for that client exists, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never sets a `type`, so `DefaultPolicyEvaluator` skips type-scoped policies. Set `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` on the resource so those policies participate in evaluation.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:136-144`

testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants all scopes at once, masking wrong-scope regressions — Because every scope is granted at once, `ClientPermissionsV2` could evaluate the wrong scope and the test would still pass: negatives still throw and post-grant operations still succeed. Create one permission per scope (`MAP_ROLES`, then `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`), or assert intermediate negative states between grants.

V2-enabled cleanup skipped: guard ignores ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 — With V2 enabled and the old flag off, removal cleanup is silently skipped while V2 keeps creating per-object permission resources, so stale policies can re-apply to a future object reusing the id. If V2 doesn't clean this up elsewhere, include `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` in the guard.

Login cache invalidation skipped when org-aware wrapper masks IDP login eligibility — When the organization is disabled, the org-aware wrapper's `isEnabled()` makes `getLoginPredicate()` false, so updates like removing `BROKER_PUBLIC` or hiding or disabling the IDP skip invalidation and stale `.idp.login` caches serve a hidden broker after re-enabling. Evaluate the predicate on the unwrapped model, e.g. via `idpDelegate.getByAlias()`.

Login cache uses empty-string sentinel that collides with empty organizationId — When a call passes an empty-string `organizationId`, the wrong result lands under the `""` key and later `null`-filter lookups skip the re-fetch, returning an empty list until invalidation. Use a non-colliding sentinel like `getByOrganization`'s `-1.-1`, or normalize empty strings to `null`.

isEnabled re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean lacks test coverage — If this `isEnabled()` filter broke, the suite would still pass, since `testCacheIDPForLogin` calls `getForLogin` directly and never renders through the bean. Add a test path that exercises `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, or assert on the models it resolves.

TableWidgetVisualization renders hardcoded empty data under flag — Organizations with the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag see completely empty table widgets because the hardcoded props discard the fetched `result.data` and `result.meta`. Pass the real data, meta, and derived columns until the new visualization is wired up.
Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb event timestamps (ms) — Convert error timestamps to milliseconds (rrweb convention, see src/sentry/replays/testutils.py) before merging.

Hidden attributes are shown when search query is empty — When the user isn't searching, the early return skips the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter entirely, so `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are rendered — the exact case the hiding was added for. Apply the filter before the empty-query early return.

Mutual-exclusion validators treat falsy 0 as absent, accepting age+timestamp together — `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` test presence with truthiness, but 0 is valid for both fields, so a report with `age: 0` plus a timestamp is accepted with 200 instead of rejected with 422. Check membership explicitly, e.g. `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`.

None max_segment_id fixture is mocked out, leaving the fix untested — The `None` fixture never reaches the fixed code because the mocked `delete_matched_rows` is the only caller of `_make_recording_filenames`, so reverting the fix would still pass. Cover the `None` case with an unmocked test of `delete_matched_rows`.

Error IDs paired with wrong event data due to positional zip of nodestore results — A backend that omits missing IDs or returns rows out of order silently pairs each error ID with the wrong event data, since the positional zip assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` preserves order and completeness. Look up by key with `events.get(node_id)` instead of `events.values()`.

submit() queries cluster memory info once per buffer, duplicating blocking Redis INFO calls — The blocking cluster-wide Redis INFO round-trip in `buffer.get_memory_info()` runs once per buffer on the consumer loop, so duplicated I/O grows with process count while the resulting ratio is unchanged. Every buffer shares the same Redis cluster, so query it once and reuse the result.

record_stored_segments runs one sequential Redis pipeline per buffer in submit — A batch submit that previously took one Redis round trip now takes one sequential pipeline per buffer, so latency grows with process count. Aggregate the zcard sampling into a single pipeline over all assigned shards instead of calling `record_stored_segments()` per buffer.

N flusher processes each use the full max-flush-segments budget — Each buffer computes `max_segments_per_shard` from its own shard subset, so total flush work reaches N times `max-flush-segments` and Redis backpressure only trips at N times the intended backlog. Divide the global budget across processes, deriving the per-shard page size from the total shard count.

`max_processes or ...` treats explicit 0 as missing, silently maximizing parallelism — Passing `--flusher-processes 0` silently spawns one process per shard, the opposite of the requested limit, because the truthiness test swallows 0. Use an `is not None` check and validate a minimum of 1 on the option.

Patched-out sleep makes flusher wait a no-op — This wait never happens because the test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op earlier, so the race the comment targets stays unfixed. Poll until `messages` is non-empty instead of sleeping.

Test only checks total shard count, not distribution across processes — If the mapping ever assigned all four shards to a single process, `total_shards` would still equal 4 and every assertion would pass. Assert the distribution itself, for example that each of the two processes received shards in `process_to_shards_map`.

Hung thread-based flusher is duplicated on restart instead of being stopped — Threads cannot be killed, so skipping `kill()` still leaves the hung thread polling its shards while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second one, and both produce duplicate segment payloads. Stop or disable the old thread first, or skip the restart and surface the failure.

Metric tag key `shards` inconsistent with `shard` used elsewhere — Dashboards or alerts querying one emit site will miss or split the data because the other flusher metrics tag the same value as `shard`. Use `shard` here too so all four emit sites agree.

AssignmentSource dict with datetime `queued` breaks Celery enqueue and round-trip — The raw datetime in `queued` isn't JSON-serializable, so enqueueing fails; over a JSON hop, `from_dict` swallows the `TypeError` and returns None, silently dropping the source so the inbound assignment syncs back to the same integration — the cycle this PR prevents. Serialize `queued` in `to_dict` and parse it in `from_dict`.

AssignmentSource.queued defaults to import-time timestamp, not construction time — Every `AssignmentSource` gets the same stale timestamp from module import instead of its actual queue time, corrupting `queued` for all consumers, including `to_dict` payloads sent to the sync task. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead of a bare default.

OAuth state uses deterministic pipeline.signature, enabling CSRF — An attacker can derive the constant `state` and forge a callback that binds their own GitHub code as `github_authenticated_user` in a victim's pipeline, defeating the user-match check. Generate a random uuid4 token per pipeline and bind it into the pipeline state instead.

Missing sender key in integration metadata causes unhandled KeyError — Older integrations can lack a `sender` key in `integration.metadata`, so the check raises an unhandled `KeyError` — a 500 instead of the graceful `error(...)` page other paths return. Read it with `.get()` and treat a missing sender as an invalid installation request.

gettext applied to variable in error() prevents extraction of error strings — The literals passed by callers never sit inside a `_(...)` call, so makemessages cannot extract them and users get untranslated English in every locale. Wrap each literal in `_()` at the call sites and drop the `_(error_short)` re-wrap in `error()`.

Unwrapped get_user_info call raises unhandled exception on GitHub API failure — Any GitHub API failure makes `get_user_info` raise as a generic 500, so the postMessage failure handshake never fires — unlike the wrapped token exchange right above. Wrap the call in try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on exception.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated — Detectors using this handler now raise `TypeError` when instantiated in `process_detectors`, since `StatefulDetectorHandler` leaves `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` unimplemented. Implement them as no-op stubs until the stateful detector abstraction is built for metric alerts.

build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value parameter, weakening fixtures — Because the expected occurrence never reflects the actual value, these fixtures still pass if `evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the wrong value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Use `value` in the occurrence (e.g. `evidence_data`) with the true per-group value at each call site, or drop the parameter.

get_monitor_environment_context returns untransformed monitor config — The monitor context sent with the incident occurrence carries the raw `schedule_type` enum instead of the readable display value, because the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` rather than the transformed copy. Return the enriched `config` local instead.
